About these tests and their limits

Three text-only tasks. Driftproof wrote the suite from the pinned skill description and README. These are not author-supplied tests. External tools, generated media and deployed services were not tested.

The eval account's configuration was read and found clean before and after each run, not during it.

Most installed first, as recorded by Skills.sh. Each result compares answers with the skill to answers without it. Each result covers 3 text-only tasks.

find-skills vercel-labs/skills

Answering model: Sonnet 5.5

Three text-only tasks: Clearly hurt.

Read test record

Why this result?

At least one task got worse. That takes priority over the overall average.

The skill clearly hurt: 0.853 with it and 0.944 without, on 3 test tasks.

search: lower scores with the skill. Compare task scores

Task score bands: search (separated-down): with skill 0.75 plus or minus 0; without skill 0.95 plus or minus 0.05.

A band is the average score plus or minus the recorded spread. These task bands, not the overall averages, determine the result.

0.853 with the skill and 0.944 without; on at least one of the 3 test tasks, the two ranges of scores (the average plus or minus one spread) did not overlap, and the gap was at least 0.05.

Test details and sources
How this result was decided

The reader applies the task rule, with a separated-down task taking precedence. Overall means do not determine the verdict. Bands show the mean plus or minus the recorded spread; point bands can reflect score quantization.

  • search: separated-down. With skill 0.75 plus or minus 0; without skill 0.95 plus or minus 0.05.
  • missing: underpowered. With skill 0.86 plus or minus 0.065192; without skill 0.883333 plus or minus 0.116905.
  • scope: underpowered. With skill 0.95 plus or minus 0.070711; without skill 1 plus or minus 0.

How we test a skill

A skill gives an AI extra instructions. We ask: do those instructions improve its written answers?

  1. The task Same question. Same AI.

    Driftproof writes tasks from the skill description.

    Give the AI a task
  2. The comparison Change the instructions
    With the skill Written answer
    Without the skill Written answer

    Repeat both ways to see how much answers vary.

  3. The result Judge each task
    Haiku 5.5 scores the answers

    A clear drop on any task takes priority. Otherwise, a better task can mean the skill helped. When answers vary too much, we cannot settle the result.

These tests cover written answers, not installation, tool use or how useful a skill is in general.
